title: Deterministic complexity lower bound for equality
statement:
For every natural number $n \ge 1$, the deterministic communication complexity of the $n$-bit equality function satisfies
\[
  n + 1 \;\le\; D(\mathrm{equality}_n),
\]
where $\mathrm{equality}_n$ is the Boolean function on $\mathrm{BoolInput}\,n \times \mathrm{BoolInput}\,n$ that returns $\mathtt{true}$ exactly when Alice's input equals Bob's input.
replaced:
For every $n \ge 1$,
\[
  n + 1 \;\le\; D(\mathrm{equality}_n).
\]
The key argument is that any monochromatic rectangle that contains a diagonal
pair $(x, x)$ must equal the singleton $\{(x,x)\}$, so any valid partition
of the input matrix into monochromatic rectangles contains at least $2^n + 1$
pieces, requiring $n + 1$ bits to index.
